title: The Twin Sisters: Umkhen and Umiam (Ka Umkhen Bad Umiam)
cultural_context: The ancient mythological ballad of two sister rivers racing from the heights of Shillong Peak down toward the plains.
lyrics_khasi:
Arngut ki shipara,
Ka Umkhen bad Umiam,
Ki la mih na Lum Shillong
Ban ia phet sha madan;
Kawei ka la phet sting
Ha ryngkat ka jingkmen,
Kawei pat ka la klet
Ban iaid beit sha la thmuh.

Haba Umiam ka la poi
Bad iohi ba la kut ka jingphet,
Ka la jaw ki ummat
Ba sngewsih ha la dohnud;
Ki ummat jong ka
Ki la pynlong ia ka wah,
Ba ngi khot Ka Umiam
Wah ba tuid jong ki jingrwai.
lyrics_english:
Two river sisters born of one mother,
Umkhen and Umiam,
Set forth from Shillong Peak
To race toward the plains below;
One dashed swift and nimble
Amid joyous laughter,
While the other tarried
Meandering along the cliffs.

When Umiam reached the valley
And saw the race was lost,
She shed copious tears
Grieving in her heart;
Those precious tears of hers
Formed the magnificent river,
Which we call Umiam,
The waters of immortal song.

khasi: Ki la mih na Lum Shillong
Ban iaid beit sha la thmuh.
english: Two river sisters born of one mother,
To race toward the plains below;

khasi: Bad iohi ba la kut ka jingphet,
Ki la pynlong ia ka wah,
Wah ba tuid jong ki jingrwai.
english: And saw the race was lost,
